title: EASTER EGG HUNTS
full_story:
Saturday weather permitting there will be 3 Easter Egg Hunts in Clay County.

The day starts with the Clay City Civics Easter Egg Hunt at 10 am at the Clay City Ball Diamonds.  Age groups will be birth to 3, 4 to 7, and 8 to 11.  There will be multiple prizes for each age group.

Then at 1 pm the Flora American Legion will have an Easter Egg Hunt at Charley Brown Park.  The age categories will be 2 to 4, 5 to 7 and 8 to 10 year olds.

The Louisville Rotary Club’s will have their Annual Easter Egg Hunt Saturday at 2 pm at the Louisville Park.  There will be a raffle for 4 tricycles and bicycles.

The Easter Egg Hunt is for all children 12 years of age and under.

Parents are reminded to bring an Easter basket or other container for kids to gather their eggs.

title: IOWA MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
On Tuesday afternoon, at approximately 1:45 pm, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office was contacted by the Iowa Department of Corrections in reference to a parolee who had an outstanding warrant, had removed his ankle monitor and was currently in the Clay City area.

As multiple deputies were responding to the area, one of the deputies observed the suspect’s vehicle traveling west on Highway 50 at Dutch Hale Road.  The deputy continued to follow the vehicle until additional units could arrive to assist with the stop.  The vehicle turned north onto Olive Street and then west on Gary Hagen Drive at which time the Deputy, Sheriff and Flora Police Department Officers conducted a felony traffic stop on the vehicle.  The driver was taken into custody without incident.  The passenger was briefly detained and released from the stop a short time later.

As a result of the stop Derek Mykyl Luna, 31, of Davenport, Iowa, was arrested on a warrant for the offense of Parole Violation/Escape.  Records also indicated that Luna was required to register as a Sex Offender.  Luna appeared in Clay County Court Wednesday and waived extradition.  Luna will remain in custody pending transportation back to the Iowa Department of Corrections.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: 6K FOR WATER
full_story:
The 2026 6k for Water will be held on Saturday, May 16th for walkers and runners from all over Southern Illinois.  This is the 10th year for Flora’s 6k for Water where people come together to raise money for clean water.  703 million people worldwide lack access to clean water.

Flora’s 6k for Water partners with the Christian Humanitarian Organization, World Vision.  In the past 9 years, Flora has raised over $60,000 for efforts that dig wells, build rain catchments, teach hygiene and more through World Vision.

6 kilometers or 3.7 miles, is the average distance that women and children all over the world walk daily for water.  As a result, children do not get the chance to go to school, they have the fear of being kidnapped and being trafficked.  Clean water within a village equals freedom from those things.  Nearly 800 children die each day from water-related illnesses.  You can help bring clean water to these communities.  World Vision reaches a new person with clean water every 10 seconds.

Sign up for the 6k at https://global6k.worldvision.org/teams/Flora2026

The race begins at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.  No need to attend FCC to join.  This is a community event.

Each registration equals clean water for 1 person for the rest of their life.

The Flora 6k for Water will be held on Saturday, May 16th, at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.

title: WORKMAN ON FORBES
full_story:

title: REDUCED RATE LABS
full_story:
Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics will be hosting their popular “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” beginning April 15th through April 30th.  You may at any time pick up a voucher at the Clay County Hospital, or at the Flora, Louisville or Clay City Clinics during regular business hours.

The blood draws must be completed April 15th through April 30th.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday – Friday, 7 am – 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am -11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher. The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” April 15th through April 30th.

title: 5th ANNUAL MASONIC AUCTION
full_story:
The 5th Annual Flora Masonic Lodge Auction will take place Saturday, May 30th at 10:00 am at the Clay County Fairgrounds in Charley Brown Park.

Anyone can donate, to make a donation call 618-843-3815.  Checks and money orders should be made out to the Shriners Hospital and mailed to Don Fry at 323 East 4th Street in Flora.  Donations will be accepted within a 50-mile radius of Flora.  The auction flyer also contains a QR Code that can be scanned to make a donation directly to the Shriner’s Hospital.  The auction never fails to offer many useful and intriguing items.  Dagg’s Auction Service will be the auctioneer.

title: EIU ROOM AND BOARD RATE
full_story:
Eastern Illinois University’s student government is taking a look at a proposed price increase before it gets passed up the line to the Board of Trustees.

Matt Beerman, Vice President for Business Affairs, said EIU is proposing a 5% increase in how much students pay for room and board.  That equates to a $300 to $400 increase.

With a new collective bargaining agreement for staff, labor costs are going up and so are food prices, according to Beerman.

Interim Housing Director Jeremy Alexander said the new proposal is the most logical way to address those increases, given how the budget shakes out.

“Most of our budget is the room and board.  So that’s about 80% of our entire revenue,” Alexander said.  “So the cost does break down for the students living in the residence halls most. That’s the cost we look at increasing.”

title: FORD RECALL
full_story:
Ford Motor Company is recalling 254-thousand vehicles due to a software issue.  The recall is for 2022-to-2025 Lincoln Navigator, 2024-to-2025 Lincoln Nautilus, 2025 Lincoln Aviator, and 2025 Ford Explorer vehicles.

The problem is with a component that interprets video captured by the vehicle that can unexpectedly reset and cause the loss of the rearview camera and disrupt driver-assistance features.  Those include lane-keeping assist, blind spot monitoring, and pre-collision assist.
